title: Wild emotional hook in the first second.
check: Watch 0 to 1 s with sound off. Record what frame 0.0 s shows. It must be a strong emotion or an odd event. In a format with a person, R20 applies.

title: Cause comes before effect on screen. Show the action, then the result, then who reacts. In a format with a person, the reaction face of R20 comes first. Then the order is action, result, reaction, all by 3 s.
check: Step through 0 to 3 s. No character appears without a reason. No object is already broken.
origin: Sitcom: door fell, people appeared at 0:02.

title: Change the camera angle, not only the zoom.
check: Look at the frames: the scene-cut filter cannot see a zoom. About one new angle or pose every 2.5 s. Cuts differ in height, pose or distance. A side change stays on one side of the 180-degree line (R21).
origin: "Different left and right views, not slow zooms."

title: The same person must show different poses and angles.
check: Same face, outfit and hair across all shots. At least 3 poses.

title: Show problem, agitation, then solution. Make the agitation hurt and be funny.
check: Mark the three beats on the timeline. Agitation has at least 3 quick cuts, one prop each.

title: No dead gaps. No silent still over 0.3 s. Tail after the last sound under 0.3 s.
check: `ad-audio-qa` R6_dead_audio is a coarse guard: FAIL on any stretch >= 1.5 s below -60 LUFS (see `ad-video-editing/references/audio-qa.md`). `freezedetect=n=-60dB:d=0.3` crossed with `silencedetect=n=-35dB:d=0.25` for the picture side is the gate.

title: Speed up the picture, not the voice. Normal speech pace.
check: `ad-audio-qa` R7_speech_pace: true WPS <= 3.4 from the whisper transcript is the tool alarm; the hand target stays 2 to 3 words per second (see `ad-video-editing/references/audio-qa.md`). Average shot length: 1.5 to 2.2 s for a lo-fi story (the gate in `qa.md`), 1.2 to 1.5 s only for a fast punch edit. No shot over 2.5 s.

title: Voice, face and ethnicity must match.
check: OWNER CHECK: a person listens to each voice with the face. No automatic check is reliable: on our own videos (1 rejected voice against 11 accepted, a small sample), neither per-line pitch spread nor a speaker embedding separated them. `ad-audio-qa` only prints R8_voice_consistency OWNER CHECK when a character's line pitch spread is above 1.25 (see `ad-video-editing/references/audio-qa.md`); it never fails. Log the voice id per character and have a person listen.

title: A story the viewer can follow. It is personal and coherent, in the first person, as a dramatization. It makes no factual claim.
check: Read the captions alone. They tell one story in the first person.

title: Captions have spaces. At most 3 words. Time them to the audio.
check: Measure the pixel gap: at least 14 px of clear gap between words at 1080 px. `ad-audio-qa` R10_caption_sync: median offset <= 300 ms and >= 70% within 300 ms of speech onsets is the tool alarm; the hand target stays 0.15 s (see `ad-video-editing/references/audio-qa.md`).

title: Mouth movement matches speech. Mouths close in laugh breaks.
check: Manual spot check until measured: mouth movement starts within 100 to 200 ms of voice onset (see `ad-video-editing` qa.md section 6). Where a lip-landmark tool ran, give its correlation (0.4 or more) and the tool name. List each failing line.

title: Never cut to a static image that makes no sense.
check: Check each cut. Every shot has motion or a reason to hold.

title: Back-and-forth dialogue is wanted. Keep it and add more.
check: Count speaker changes. At least 4 in a sitcom.

title: Sound is required. The ad also works muted.
check: `ad-audio-qa` R14_sound_and_cuts and sfx_onset_80ms need `--sfx-stem` (a wav of the sfx alone: leave the laugh track out, it does not land on cuts): FAIL "Sound is required" when the stem has no onsets, else FAIL when under 80% of the sfx onsets land within 80 ms of a picture cut (see `ad-video-editing/references/audio-qa.md`). A cut with no sfx is fine. A voice onset does not count as a sound event. Pass beat times that are not picture cuts with `--cuts`. sfx_vs_voice needs `--voice-stem` too. pacing.md: sfx only on events, never one per cut. Play with sound off. The story and the offer still read. Ship both files.

title: Hold the object identity. A phone stays a phone.
check: Compare held objects in frames across the clip.

title: Lo-fi organic look. No logo. No text except captions, the dramatization tag and one end card with the offer.
check: Look at the frames. No logo, no studio polish.

title: Housing safety. "dramatization" label. No invented numbers. No real people. No children.
check: Run the policy lint on all text and captions.

title: Cost goes down each time. Report cost per video by stage.
check: Compare with the last video of the same format. Explain any rise.

title: Do not show an event the video model cannot render. Show damage another way.
check: Render one clip first. Look at 3 frames of the event. No duplicate objects (two doors), no melting. If it fails, change the beat (cracking wall, falling plaster).

title: In a format with a person, the first frame is that person's reaction face. The cause follows in the next shot or two (see R2). This replaces the 0.0 s check in R1 for those formats.
check: Frame 0.0 s: a face, eyes and mouth readable, emotion matches the hook. The cause is on screen by 3 s.

title: Keep screen direction. Each person stays on the same side of the frame in every shot. Change the angle on one side of the 180-degree line. Do not cross it.
check: List left/right per shot for each person. No swap, including cutaways.
origin: Street interview: host moved from right to left.

title: A conversation looks like one: eyelines, head turns, small hand gestures, a slow push-in on the punchline. Do the push-in in the edit as a crop. Ask the model for small gestures only.
check: Per talking shot: where does the person look? Count eyeline-matched reverse shots (at least 1). Note the crop push-in. OWNER CHECK for how natural it looks.
origin: "Talk as if to someone, more hand movement, zoom in on the guy."

title: Captions never look jumbled.
check: Compile `swiftc -O ocr.swift` (macOS Vision, `VNRecognizeTextRequest`, accurate, language correction off). Run it on one frame per caption from the final render. Retry once on an `e5rt` crash. Character error rate (edit distance divided by expected length, upper case, spaces collapsed) 0.10 or less. Do not run `swift ocr.swift` (it hangs).

title: Show the tool of the format. A street interview shows the microphone in the host's hand. Name the mic in the motion prompt and include it in the R15 frame comparison.
check: Frame check: mic visible in every host shot, same shape in each.

title: A horror-comic variant needs a scare beat: something moves behind a door, a sting, a reaction. Then it resolves as a joke.
check: Mark the beat on the timeline. A sting starts within 0.2 s of the beat, then a reaction shot. OWNER CHECK for how scary it feels.

title: A personal story has a clear hook: the loss, the place, the trust that broke, the surprise. The offer is on the end card. The narrator never says the product worked. See R9 and R17.
check: Caption read: one sentence per beat, in that order. No line claims a result.
origin: "I spent all my savings on this house ... a slick agent gave me a lien ... someone lives there."
